title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: handle client cancel/disconnect + reconnect/resume + server timeouts (OpenAI compat)
author: Aisha Patel
commits: a1f3b2c: initial implementation of lifecycle control hooks and server timeout plumbing
d4e5f6a: add reconnect/resume token protocol + KV-cache resume support
b7c8d9e: integrate OpenAI-compat reconnect events and streaming error codes
f0e1d2c: tests, metrics, and docs updates
c3b4a5d: fix flake in stream teardown path and add backoff for reconnect attempts
description:
Context: customers and internal users have reported two classes of streaming issues: (1) client-initiated cancels or abrupt TCP disconnects that left server-side resources allocated and KV cache entries pinned, leading to OOM and elevated p99 latency; (2) flaky reconnect/resume behavior when network blips occur, plus inconsistent behavior across our OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR implements end-to-end streaming lifecycle controls: explicit client cancel handling, robust disconnect detection + graceful teardown, reconnect/resume protocol with resume tokens and KV-cache state rehydration, and server-side timeouts to avoid resource leaks.

What changed: single-string summary of design and changes: added a LifecycleManager component that centralizes stream state (ACTIVE, CANCELED, DISCONNECTED, RESUMING, TERMINATED) and exposes hooks for handlers and the KV cache; new OpenAI-compat event types and status codes for resume/reconnect; reconnect protocol that issues opaque resume tokens to clients on disconnect and accepts resume requests that rebind token to new connection and rehydrate KV cache; server-side configurable idle and grace timeouts (defaults: idle=30s, resume_grace=120s) and an explicit cancellation path that frees memory, cancels batch slots, and emits trace/metric events.

Design notes and compatibility: resume tokens are opaque and short-lived (configurable TTL). The implementation preserves backwards compatibility: clients that do not speak reconnect/resume receive the same stream termination events as before. OpenAI-compat layer now maps our reconnect/resume lifecycle to standard OpenAI-style 'error'/'restart' events and adds a new 'resume_token' field in the final event envelope when applicable. We maintained existing SDK behavior by adding helpers in the Python/TS SDKs (non-breaking additions).

Testing and metrics: added unit and integration tests covering cancel path, abrupt disconnect, resume success/failure, and server timeout enforcement. CI includes a new workflow that runs streaming tests with simulated network blips. New metrics: streaming.session_lifecycle_state, streaming.resume_attempts_total, streaming.resume_success_ratio, streaming.grace_timeout_expirations.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime config; staged rollout to canary region for 48h with increased tracing. SRE will monitor streaming.grace_timeout_expirations and resume_success_ratio. If regressions are observed we will disable resume (fallback to previous behavior) via runtime flag.

Checklist:
- [x] Lifecycle manager core implementation
- [x] OpenAI-compat protocol mapping
- [x] KV cache rehydration on resume
- [x] Server-side idle/grace timeouts + configuration
- [x] SDK helpers and docs update
- [x] Unit/integration tests + CI workflow
- [x] Metrics and dashboard for rollout
changes_summary: Centralized stream lifecycle state machine + reconnect/resume tokens, server idle/grace timeouts to avoid leaks, OpenAI compatibility mapping for resume events, SDK helpers and tests. Configurable defaults: idle=30s, resume_grace=120s.
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Please ensure resume tokens are rotated and cannot be replayed. Also request a small e2e test that simulates resume after kv cache eviction.
Aisha Patel: Added token rotation and single-use semantics; updated tests to simulate eviction and verified resume fails fast with appropriate error code.
Lin Chen: Left a nit about naming 'DISCONNECTED' vs 'INTERRUPTED' state — ok to leave as-is for now but file docs note.
Samir Gupta: Observability looks good. Please ensure SLO alert thresholds are documented in the rollout notes.
Aisha Patel: Added SLO alert guidance and a dashboard panel; increased unit test coverage for teardown path.
release_notes: Add streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel handling, graceful disconnect teardown, reconnect/resume via opaque tokens, and server idle/grace timeouts. OpenAI compatibility updates include resume_token in final envelopes and mapped event codes.
